ids_decide_ctx_builds_per_ack.evidence: QEMU validate.sh at the lazy decide-context commit: a plain TCP ACK through packet::verdict builds no decide() context (before, one was built on every call of every rule tier, 4 built-in tiers per packet: read from the code, not measured)

ids_pack64_prog_runs_other_port.evidence: QEMU validate.sh at the ADR 0067 X1 step 1 commit: a 64-rule dst-port tier, one packet to an unnamed port; 64 programs ran with guards off, 1 (the rule with no guard) with guards on

ids_tcp_tier_prog_runs_ack.evidence: QEMU validate.sh at the ADR 0067 X1 step 2 commit: the built-in TCP-flag tier on a plain ACK; 4 programs ran with guards off, 0 with byte guards on

l2_stateful_clock_reads_tcp.evidence: QEMU validate.sh at the ARP-check clock commit: a unicast TCP data frame through l2_stateful_verdict reads the seconds clock 0 times (was 1: the ARP binding check's argument was computed for every frame)

nat_newflow_scan_max.evidence: QEMU validate.sh at the ADR 0067 E3 commit: free stack + fresh mark + bounded 32-slot sweep (was 4096)

nat_rewrite_csum_bytes.evidence: QEMU validate.sh at the ADR 0067 E4 commit: RFC 1624 incremental update over the rewritten words of a 1,500-byte TCP segment (was 1500)

wasm_events_per_round_trip.evidence: QEMU validate.sh at the ADR 0067 X2a step 2 commit: 16 flow-event records answered by a signed wasip1 module in one EL0 round trip, one packed verdict word back (was 1 input per round trip)
